title: Enhancer control of promoter activity and variability via frequency modulation of clustered transcriptional bursts.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Zenodo API record 17572944 (licence CC-BY-4.0): one file, tracks.csv, 169,065,928 bytes (over the 50 MB cap, so not fully downloaded). Ranged reads of the first 300 KB and the last 265 KB: 12 columns (unique_id, clone, frame, x, y, mean_spot, mean_spot_bleach, corrected_intensity, mean_localbackground, mean_localbackground_bleach, mean_completecell, spotdetected). Clone names such as 5G7 and 5E10 seen. unique_id goes past 10,000 and frame reaches 600. There is no enhancer-position column and no intensity units are given (raw camera counts).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: 30 s frame interval over 5 h; 3–7 biological replicates per cell line; 1,000–2,500 tracks per line, coming from about 200–400 cells per condition; mapping of clone to enhancer distance (only 5G7 = −5 kb and 5F11 = −149 kb are named in the text I searched). I did not count the total number of clones or rows in the full file. Raw images are available only on request.

a1_downloadable.note: Processed intensity tracks are openly on Zenodo under CC-BY-4.0 (169 MB CSV, checked via the API and ranged reads). Raw images are 'on request' only, but those aren't needed.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: The only natural target, enhancer position, is not in the file: it would have to be mapped from the clone name using the paper's figures. The other candidate, 'spotdetected' (burst on/off), is a computed detection call, not a measured outcome.

a3_inputs_present.note: Per-frame intensity traces are present as numbers (seen in the file head and tail).

a4_units_stated.note: Intensities are unnamed camera counts with no units. The frame interval (30 s) comes only from the paper text.

a5_enough_rows.note: About 1M frame rows (estimated from file size), but the independent unit is the clonal line (enhancer position). Each line is a single clone with about 200–400 cells, and there are only a handful of lines. Holding out whole clones leaves far fewer than 400 labelled units.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Fits easily in RAM, and no GPU is needed.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Not fully verified. The 10,000+ track IDs I saw are consistent with the paper's 1,000–2,500 tracks per line across several lines.

a8_label_provenance.note: 'spotdetected' comes from Trackpy (a spot-tracking tool) plus a filter applied to these same intensities, so it is computed from the features. Enhancer position is a real experimental setting but has the A2/A5 problems above.

existing_models.name: Paper's own double-regime two-state promoter model (BurstingDynamicsInference, a mechanistic stochastic model)
existing_models.score_and_split: Fitted to burst and gap-duration survival curves for each clone; not a predictive train/test model.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Which molecular mechanism sets the switch from the low-frequency to the high-frequency burst regime.

existing_models.name: DART (a convolutional plus LSTM neural network that turns MS2 traces into promoter on/off states; bioRxiv 2025)
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported to beat hidden Markov model binarisation on simulated and published traces; I did not retrieve its numbers.

existing_models.name: BurstInfer (a compound hidden Markov model for MS2 kinetics; Bioinformatics 2022)
existing_models.score_and_split: Kinetic-parameter inference validated on simulated data; no held-out split.

existing_models.name: BurstDECONV (signal deconvolution of live-cell bursting; NAR 2023)

backbone.name: none (no pretrained foundation model for MS2 intensity time series)

integration.partner_dataset: Companion Nature Genetics paper 'The genomic position of an enhancer modulates bursting dynamics of the cognate promoter' (s41588-026-02693-w), not inspected
integration.join_key: none shared; different constructs and cell lines
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Does the way burst frequency depends on enhancer distance carry over between independent engineered loci? That can't be answered from the few clones here.

controls.positive_control: Burst frequency in the −5 kb clone (about 7 per trace) should exceed the −149 kb clone (about 1), as stated in the paper.
controls.external_validation: None joinable; the companion paper uses a different construct.

honest_claim_h3: A model could only say that traces from a few specific clonal lines of one mouse embryonic stem cell construct are distinguishable. It could not show that it learned how enhancer distance shapes bursting.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use single-cell live-imaging traces of RNA production to predict how far the controlling enhancer sits from the gene.
plain_idea.train_on: Per-cell fluorescence traces (one frame every 30 s for 5 h) of nascent RNA at one engineered gene. Roughly 10,000 tracks, but they come from only a handful of clonal lines.
plain_idea.predict: The enhancer's position (the clone it belongs to). That is set by the experiment, but it isn't a column: it has to be mapped from clone names using the paper.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: It would test whether the timing of single-cell bursts encodes regulatory distance. But with only a few distances, any classifier mostly learns clone identity, so little would be learned.

ml_idea: Classify or regress enhancer–promoter distance from single-cell MS2 bursting traces (MS2 is a tag that makes newly made RNA glow). This is not viable: there are only a handful of clones, so a leave-one-clone-out split leaves a few labelled units.

effort.compute_note: Estimated from the 169 MB file size; nothing was timed.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count distinct 'clone' values in tracks.csv and map each to an enhancer distance. If there are fewer than about 15 clones, the project is dead.

verdict_reason: This is a mechanistic study of a handful of clonal lines. The real independent unit is the enhancer position, of which there are only a few, so A5 fails. Enhancer position isn't a column and has to be mapped from clone names (A2), the only per-frame label is a computed burst call (A8), and intensities have no units (A4).
